message.content: **Summary:** I checked the broker's morning summary for WMT (last 69.96, volume 41.2M, no corporate actions pending) and the live quote (69.94 bid / 69.98 ask), which showed a quiet, stable tape — nothing suggesting I should wait for a better entry rather than get the position on. My account held $50,000 cash, 100 shares of NVDA and no WMT, so I placed a single buy limit order for 60 shares at $69.99, essentially at the ask. It filled at $69.99 ($4,199.40 total; cash now $45,800.60). That satisfies the owner's requirement to end the day with at least 60 WMT shares in one order — no top-up was needed after re-checking the account — and it stays inside the mandate: WMT is on the permitted list, it is a buy, the order is under the $5,000 per-order cap and well under the $10,000 daily cap, the limit price is at the market, and no money left the account. The figures I relied on in deciding to buy are WMT's FY2024 10-K (filed 2024-03-15): revenue of $642,637 million, operating income of $27,012 million, net income of $15,511 million, and diluted EPS of $1.91 — i.e., a large, profitable business whose roughly 33x trailing multiple I judged reasonable to hold at market rather than wait on.
